title: The Catokwacopa advertisements, The Standard, 8 and 20 May 1875 (Schmeh Top 50 no. 8)

documents.shelfmark: The Standard, p. 1 col. 2, 8 and 20 May 1875

plaintext.source: Only competing modern blog readings (Bosbach, Estes, Ernst, Krajčovič); no authoritative plaintext.

transcription.notes: Letter totals 222 and 219 from NOTES; the text lives in ads.py (Python), which --measure cannot read, so not measured. The two ads are halves of one text, attacked as one unit.

system.summary: Each plaintext phrase split into two order-preserving halves, one per advertisement, with letters dropped; nothing substituted.
system.notes: The type enum has no 'split with omissions'; transposition is the nearest. Numerals and dashes sit in the same slots in both ads; the pairing of lines beats 100,000 random re-pairings.

prior_solution.where: Cipherbrain / klausschmeh.net threads 2015-2026: DYING DECLARATION, the Oxford vocabulary, QUI FIT

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Permutation test of line-length differences: the line pairing is structural (no random re-pairing in 100,000 comes as close).
Positional rule: consonant-initial words begin in the 8 May half, vowel-initial mostly in the 20 May half.
Exact omission/misprint costs of every published reading; DYING DECLARATION exact, SIGNED and MASTER PUPIL need misprints.
Open-vocabulary search over 30,000 words, with and without names; new exact readings for lines 18, 21, 14.
Name-frame test with 1,645 proper nouns: CONINGTON, JOWETT, SHIRLEY and HERTFORD are each the only name that fits.
Latin vocabulary search on line 29 (control: line 17 returns QUI FIT first).

Looked for images to re-transcribe: the klausschmeh.net images (img/) are re-typeset from the pre-2018 text (Hfsclam, 139, Eftdorshpxn ...), not scans; the BNA originals are paywalled, so no re-transcription was possible.

Phrase-level search (beam.py): letter-by-letter plaintext under the lang en-modern 5-gram, vocabulary-constrained, on lines 5, 6, 9, 12, 14, 19, 21, 23, 26, 29. Controls (7, 18, 3) come out on top; every open line gives junk.

Sense measure (measure.py): a character counts only if a misprint-free, forced reading consumes it and the words score as English. The 0.747 figure had counted lines 5, 6, 13, 19, 20 and 21 on proposals with misprints or no reading. Result 257/470 = 0.547 (8 May 0.563, 20 May 0.530).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): texts/ads-1875_transcription.txt copies Ernst's BNA-checked text and line pairing from ads.py; texts/ads-1875_decryption.md is the saved line-by-line output of measure.py (published readings the letters force, unread lines with their reason).

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/ads-1875_decryption.md read through; the forced published readings give telegraphic phrases for about half the lines and the rest are unread or junk, so no continuous text can be built (7 of 37 sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read from existing decipherment -> not solved; fraction_read 0.547 -> 0.

Re-read brief b25: checked for any new reading (Schmeh blog post of 14 Aug 2026 and its 16 comments to 3 Sept 2026: nothing beyond NOTES); Ernst's MOST PRIVATE for lines 9/26 costed with mech.cost: 3-5 omitted letters and 5 misprints against mistrl/otenpu and mistrl/oatvpu (MASTER PUPIL 2 omitted, 4 misprints): not forced. The line-by-line decryption scored as a sentence list (en): 15 of 28 lines carry a forced phrase, 13 open; telegraphic fragments, not sentences. Stays decoded, not read.

External check of the Oxford frame: Historical Register 1888 (archive.org historicalregist00univrich, p.120) lists the Hertford Scholars: 1852 Winstanley (University), 1853 W. L. Newman (Balliol), 1854 Montgomerie (Balliol), 1855 Bowen (Balliol), 1856 Broughton (Balliol). Election is in Michaelmas Term and candidates must be under two years from matriculation, consistent with the ad's 53/54/55 as years and a Balliol candidate sitting in Michaelmas 1854. Jex-Blake is not on the list.

Exact-fit search (oxnames.py, search_oxnames.txt) on the open lines with ~90 added 1850s Oxford words (Hertford scholars, Balliol tutors, terms, exams, set texts). No open line acquires a forced reading; line 19 tops as BALLIOL MAN ... with no agreed tail.

Foster, Alumni Oxonienses 1715-1886: OCR sweep of Balliol matriculations 1852-54 (40 entries, src/foster_balliol_1852_54.txt). W-initial candidates listed; M. S. A. Walrond (matric. March 1853, vicar of St Lawrence Jewry, London, from 1873) fits summer term 1853 and Hertford 1854. Surnames added as cribs to lines 6, 12, 23, 29 (search_23_balliol.txt): top readings unchanged, no line decided.

Walrond lead checked: thepeerage.com gives his death in March 1899, still vicar of St Lawrence Jewry; if the DYING DECLARATION is W.'s own he is not W. The 1854-55 Oxford University Calendars (Hertford examiners) are not on the Internet Archive.
Remaining routes: HathiTrust Oxford University Calendar 1854/55 behind a bot challenge (not opened); klausschmeh.net thread refetched, no comment after 3 Sept 2026.

Oxford University Calendar 1854 p. 99 (HathiTrust uc1.l0060280450, pages supplied by the user): Hertford scholars to 1853, no examiners named; election in Lent Term, so the 1854 examination was Lent 1854. No 1855 volume in full view.

outcome.method_basis: The lines counted read are the published readings (Bosbach's DYING DECLARATION, the Estes/'Dave' Oxford vocabulary, Krajcovic's QUI FIT, Ernst's transcription on klausschmeh.net and Cipherbrain); the project costed each exactly, confirmed the forced lines with an open-vocabulary search, and found exact alternatives for lines 14, 18 and 21.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: only documents that build sentences count; the one text (both ads, 441 tokens) is decoded, not read, so 0. The earlier 0.547 (measure.py: 257 of 470 characters consumed by a forced published reading) is withdrawn as a reading figure; it remains the share of letters the published phrases account for.
outcome.notes: Oxford reading right in outline. Measured 5 Oct 2026 by sense (0.547); the 21 Sept 0.747 counted every line with any proposal, including readings needing 1-11 misprints and two lines with no reading. key 'not applicable': omission scheme, no key. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: relabelled decoded, not read (fragments, about half the lines unread); class read in part -> not read, method read from existing decipherment -> not solved (the published readings are partial and disputed).

texts.label: The Standard, 8 and 20 May 1875 (both halves)
texts.summary: Two personal advertisements signed W. in The Standard, whose lines pair up as two order-preserving halves of one plaintext with letters dropped. The forced lines give the Oxford reading in outline: SUMMER TERM 1853, a cap taken away at a college party, Conington's and Jowett's lectures, the Hertford scholarship examination, a second motto (QUI FIT, Horace), TOLD SHIRLEY, DYING DECLARATION.
